title: Self-Supervised Continual Graph Learning via Adaptive Spaced Replay on Node Proxies

problem.claim: Continual graph learning must handle continuously generated graph data, including settings with abundant unlabeled data.

gap.claim: Self-supervised continual graph learning research is described as being in its infancy, while existing continual graph learning models generally rely on external supervision.

contributions.claim: Self-supervised representation models may be potentially better continual learners than supervised counterparts.
Trace is a self-supervised continual graph representation learning framework based on adaptive spaced replay on node proxies.

Trace uses a dual-system architecture with a fast-learning system for encoding current graphs and caching adaptively extracted node proxies, and a slow-learning system for adaptive spaced replay based on memory retention rates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Empirical studies find that self-supervised representation models may be potentially better continual learners than supervised counterparts.
Experiments under task-incremental and class-incremental learning settings on multiple datasets are reported to corroborate the proposed approach.

narrative_sequence.summary: Offline graph learning assumptions may not hold when graph data are generated continuously.
Existing continual graph learning models generally depend on external supervision, and self-supervised continual graph learning is presented as an early research area.
The authors report that self-supervised representation models may be better continual learners than supervised counterparts.
The paper proposes Trace, combining node-proxy memory caching through progressive clustering with adaptive spaced replay based on memory retention rates.
The abstract reports experiments in task-incremental and class-incremental settings on multiple datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates rapid encoding and knowledge acquisition from slower replay based on estimated memory retention.

interpretation.claim: Continual learning systems may benefit from coordinating fast adaptation with retention-aware rehearsal.

application.claim: For streaming graph representation learning, consider compact proxy-based memory and replay schedules that adapt to retention estimates.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract does not establish whether this design is effective across graph types, task schedules, or resource constraints beyond the reported settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
